quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, you should use ____ to show you are turning.

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to show when you are turning.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must allow for:

options.text: The longer stopping distance needed by large vehicles.
The shorter stopping distance needed by large vehicles.
The quieter noise of larger vehicles.
The faster speed of larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer stopping distance needed by large vehicles.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you can see traffic clearly.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the road?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back on the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back on the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back on the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not panic. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and gently steer back onto the road with a small turn of the wheel. Check for traffic before returning to the pavement.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crossing. Watch for people crossing the road. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass when they use sirens or horns and flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only move when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the nearest roadside and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and continue with caution.
Wait until the train has completely passed before crossing.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the train has completely passed before crossing.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if signals are not present or not working.

questions.question: ____ limit your focus, awareness, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only high blood alcohol levels can
Alcohol does not
Even small amounts of alcohol can
Only blood alcohol of 0.05 percent or higher can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even small amounts of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol reduce your focus, awareness, judgment, and memory. Your driving will suffer. You cannot drink and drive safely.

questions.question: Increase your following distance when:

options.text: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
Exiting an expressway.
Following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: Where should you go to take the Missouri driver exam?

options.text: Any Missouri State Highway Patrol testing station.
Any Department of Transportation office.
Any Missouri contract office.
The nearest high school driver education class.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any Missouri State Highway Patrol testing station.
questions.explanation: The Missouri State Highway Patrol gives the driver exam. Contact the Highway Patrol or Department of Revenue to find the testing center nearest you.

questions.question: What happens if you cause a traffic crash and do not pay for the damages?

options.text: Your driver license and/or plates will be suspended for one year.
You will save money.
Your car will be repossessed.
You must buy a new car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your driver license and/or plates will be suspended for one year.
questions.explanation: If you cause an accident and do not pay for damages, your driver license and/or vehicle plates will be suspended for one year. You can get your license and plates back before one year if you pay a fee and prove you have settled the damages.

questions.question: What headlights must you use when driving in rain?

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights.
Use parking lights.
Use no lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In rainy conditions, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and go for help.
Lay down in your car and go to sleep.
Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.
Stay in the car. You are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the car. You are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm can be unsafe.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to an open intersection, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue driving without stopping.
One driver should honk to indicate that they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, you must yield to that vehicle. You can then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the effect of driving much slower than the speed limit?

options.text: It makes you a very safe driver.
You always have the right-of-way.
You should not let following cars pass.
It may create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic around you can be hazardous. If you are on a two-lane road and driving so slowly that traffic backs up behind you, you must pull over and let other vehicles pass. Only drive significantly under the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: What should you do when you are in a travel lane on the roadway?

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp of the freeway.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: How can you reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Allow extra travel time.
Obey posted speed limits.
Use proper turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey posted speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving ability?

options.text: The same way alcohol affects it.
The same way amphetamines affect it.
The same way anger affects it.
The same way driving with teenagers affects it.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way alcohol affects it.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol have similar effects on your driving ability. Being awake for 18 hours impairs your driving about as much as having a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours impairs your driving as much as having a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: What must you do when driving near a motorcycle?

options.text: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle with the same rights as any other vehicle on the road. Give motorcyclists a full lane width. Even if there seems to be room to share a lane, the motorcycle needs space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep the night before your trip.
Taking short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: "Highway hypnosis" happens when you stare straight ahead at the road for too long and stop watching ahead, behind, and around your vehicle. This causes you to zone out and may cause you to crash into traffic that is slowing or stopping.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a detour ahead.
You must stop for flaggers.
The road ahead is closed to traffic.
Road work is happening ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road work is happening ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about construction zones. This sign tells you that road work is ahead. Slow down and drive carefully through work areas.

questions.question: How far in advance should you signal before turning right or left?

options.text: 100 feet
50 feet
35 feet
10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Use your turn signals or hand signals. This gives other drivers time to see what you plan to do.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.
Lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a road is crossing ahead. An intersection is where two roads meet.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.
Drive carefully around all other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In snow or sleet, keep your windshield and mirrors clean so you can see. Leave extra space between your vehicle and others because wet, icy roads make it harder to stop. Drive slowly and carefully around other vehicles.

questions.question: When turning, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Keep the same
Change
Decrease

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease
questions.explanation: Slow down before you turn. This helps you stay in your lane, control your vehicle, and react if something unexpected happens.
